question: Should ClawHub support the reported default OpenClaw skill names as installable registry targets, and should users install them by unscoped short name or owner-qualified official refs?
rationale: The source paths are clear, but the safe behavior depends on a maintainer-owned trust and product decision about official default skills versus community slugs and bundled local skill resolution.

options.title: Use owner-qualified official targets
options.body: Publish or verify official `@openclaw/<slug>` skill rows for the intended defaults and update OpenClaw setup/docs to use owner-qualified refs instead of ambiguous short names.

options.title: Add reserved short aliases
options.body: Reserve and route the default short names to official rows, with tests that prevent community collisions and preserve existing ambiguity behavior elsewhere.

options.title: Keep defaults local to OpenClaw
options.body: Do not make these ClawHub registry names special; update OpenClaw CLI/setup guidance so bundled defaults resolve locally or through explicit owner-qualified refs only.

recommendation.title: Use owner-qualified official targets
recommendation.body: Publish or verify official `@openclaw/<slug>` skill rows for the intended defaults and update OpenClaw setup/docs to use owner-qualified refs instead of ambiguous short names.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision touches the CODEOWNERS-listed Convex API and ClawHub CLI contract surfaces where Patrick has the strongest current history.
